summary: Backend-only regression on the N+1 optimization of GET /api/route-configs. Ran the existing suite with -n 0 (24/24 pass in 6.82s: test_route_configs.py + test_simulation.py) and added a new focused suite test_route_configs_n1_enrichment.py (4/4 pass in 1.98s) that verifies: (1) batch driver enrichment does not mix up drivers across routes with different driver_ids; (2) driver=null when a route has no driver assigned; (3) list endpoint strips heavy 'stops' and 'sim_stops' while keeping stops_count and sim_summary; (4) GET /route-configs/{id} still returns the full doc (stops + sim_stops) with enriched driver; (5) list latency < 3s. CRUD, one-route-per-driver 409, Excel stops upload, and simulation-save regressions all pass. No regressions detected.
critical_code_review_comments: list_route_configs correctly batches driver_ids via $in and passes users_map to _enrich_config, eliminating the N+1. Implementation is clean: build unique driver_ids set, single $in query with password_hash projected out, in-memory enrichment. Contract preserved (driver object shape unchanged).
Minor: to_list(1000) caps route_configs and users lists at 1000. Fine at current scale but worth documenting or paginating if the tenant grows beyond that.
seed_data_creation: Created (if missing) driver users 9901 (TEST_DrvA) and 9902 (TEST_DrvB) with password 2002 to exercise multi-driver enrichment. Test route_configs prefixed TEST_N1_* are cleaned up in teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: N+1 optimization on GET /api/route-configs is verified. The new file test_route_configs_n1_enrichment.py is the canonical regression for the batch enrichment: multi-driver isolation, driver=null case, stripping of stops/sim_stops in list vs full-doc GET, and sim_summary preservation. Run all route-config tests with -n 0 due to shared driver contention across xdist workers.
